binders: Universally quantify real constants K = bulkModulus and ρ = density, and a system in LocalDef001 K ρ.
The system supplies functions p,u : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ, interpreted as pressure and velocity, with the first argument x and second argument t.
The first transport conclusion universally quantifies x,t ∈ ℝ.
The profile conclusion universally quantifies a function f : ℝ → ℝ, a real number a = profile', and x,t ∈ ℝ.
For each point in the system assumptions, existentially quantify real derivative values pt, px, ut, ux; these witnesses lie inside the quantification over x and t.
For each asserted transport condition, existentially quantify real derivative values qt and qx at that point; these may depend on all preceding parameters, the relevant field and the point.
hypotheses: The system bundle includes ρ ≠ 0 and, for every x,t ∈ ℝ, existence of p_t(x,t), p_x(x,t), u_t(x,t), u_x(x,t), with p_t(x,t) + K u_x(x,t) = 0 and u_t(x,t) + ρ⁻¹ p_x(x,t) = 0.
Within the profile conclusion only, assume f has derivative a at x + ct, where c = √(K/ρ).
conclusions: For every x,t ∈ ℝ, w(x,t) = p(x,t) − ρc u(x,t) has both first partial derivatives at (x,t), and w_t(x,t) − c w_x(x,t) = 0.

For every f : ℝ → ℝ, a ∈ ℝ and x,t ∈ ℝ, if f has derivative a at x + ct, then the field q(ξ,τ) = f(ξ − (−c)τ) has both first partial derivatives at (x,t), satisfies q_t(x,t) − c q_x(x,t) = 0, and obeys q(x,t) = f(x + ct).
mathematical_definitions: c denotes the nonnegative real square root √(K/ρ); it is defined from the parameters, not an additional quantified or existentially chosen speed.
For a real-valued field q and real speed s, the transport predicate at (x,t) means: there exist A,B ∈ ℝ such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative A at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative B at x, and A + sB = 0.
The system predicate at (x,t) means: there exist pt,px,ut,ux ∈ ℝ such that the corresponding one-variable slices of p and u have those derivatives and pt + Kux = 0 and ut + ρ⁻¹px = 0.
The system-derived field is w(x,t) = p(x,t) − (ρc)u(x,t).
A translated profile with speed s is the function (x,t) ↦ f(x − st). For s = −c it equals f(x + ct).
All derivatives use the ordinary topology and norm on ℝ. Partial derivatives mean derivatives of one-variable slices with the other argument fixed.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any positive real constants K and ρ and any supplied system consisting of pressure and velocity functions p and u whose first space and time partial derivatives exist everywhere on ℝ² and satisfy p_t + Ku_x = 0 and u_t + ρ⁻¹p_x = 0 everywhere, let c = √(K/ρ). Then c > 0, and the field w = p − ρcu has both first partial derivatives everywhere and satisfies w_t − cw_x = 0 everywhere. Furthermore, for any real-valued profile f, any real derivative value a and any point (x,t), if f has derivative a at x + ct, then its translated field q(ξ,τ) = f(ξ − (−c)τ) has both first partial derivatives at (x,t), satisfies q_t − cq_x = 0 there, and has value q(x,t) = f(x + ct).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: K and ρ are constant real parameters, not functions of space or time. The target applies only under their strict positivity assumptions.
Space and time both range over all of ℝ. There is no restriction t ≥ 0, bounded spatial interval, boundary condition or initial condition.

The system requires first partial derivatives at every point and pointwise equations. It does not require continuous partial derivatives, joint differentiability, second derivatives or any specified function-space norm bounds.

The profile hypothesis is local: differentiability is required only at x + ct for the chosen point. For profiles not differentiable there, that conditional assertion imposes no conclusion. Global differentiability of f is not assumed.

The target quantifies over supplied systems rather than asserting existence or uniqueness of a system. The displayed constructor conditions admit constant pressure and velocity functions when ρ is nonzero, so the positive-parameter setting has no evident empty-system obstruction.
The profile field is not asserted to equal the system-derived field w. The target does not claim that every solution of the transport equation has the displayed profile form.
The transport witnesses are existential derivative values at each point. The target does not explicitly identify the profile field's derivative witnesses as ca and a.
The profile value equality is placed under the differentiability hypothesis even though the equality follows from the profile definition and real arithmetic independently of differentiability.
The encoded speed is −c and the equation is q_t − cq_x = 0. There is no conclusion about the opposite-sign combination p + ρcu or transport speed +c.
The theorem does not encode a physical interpretation, units, propagation boundaries, an existence theorem for prescribed data or a complete classification of solutions.
Real inversion and square root are totalized, but ρ > 0 and K > 0 exclude zero division and the nonpositive square-root branch in this target.
